newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast gasolines higher after Tosco fire.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast gasolines higher after Tosco fire.

text.p: U.S. West Coast wholesale gasoline prices moved notionally higher Wednesday, following an overnight fire at Tosco's 156,000 barrel-per-day refinery near San Francisco, Calif., traders said.
The fire erupted ahead of a weekly inventory figures from the American Petroleum Institute (API), and amid several planned shutdowns at the plant and others on the West Coast.

The API report reflected a drop in production caused by the region's maintenance programs. Refinery utilization was throttled back by 2.1 percentage points last week, to 82.5 of total regional capacity.
A trade for San Francisco CARB grade gasoline was heard as high as 80 cents a barrel, and 79.50 cents earlier. The deals reported were two cents firmer than Tuesday levels.
"They bumped up on strength of the fire," a trader said, adding activity was thin because of an industry function.
Los Angeles CARB was talked notionally at 77/78 cents a gallon for late January and first-week February shipments.
Late February prices were assessed around 80/81 cents, firmer because of possible supply disruptions caused by Tosco, and by a seasonal drop after winter blending ends.
